headline: Highest risk is medium: Authelia can broker OAuth/ForwardAuth flows while the sample suite has no documented runtime surfaces, so pairwise leakage and conflict are limited but interaction is under-specified.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. Authelia exposes OAuth2/OpenID Connect and ForwardAuth, but spring-integration-samples has no runtime I/O surfaces or ingestion path shown, so a prompt-injection bridge is not evidenced. Uncertainty is low enough to keep this at none rather than infer a hidden parser.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the two agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF spring-integration-samples is wrapped in a parser that treats Authelia output as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except through explicit, typed APIs.
Do not pipe Authelia responses into any instruction-following prompt.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared messages.
requires-engineering: add content filtering for instruction-like text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and may handle authentication traffic, while spring-integration-samples shows no data classes touched and no egress. With no shared workspace or sensitive data documented, leakage is possible only through unusual integration, so the blast radius appears small and not default.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same workspace, file leakage becomes plausible.
IF Authelia is configured to process sensitive identity data from the sample suite, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid shared directories between the two agents.
Store secrets outside any workspace both can read.
Review Authelia egress destinations before enabling it.
requires-engineering: isolate each agent in separate containers or VMs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make outbound API calls, but spring-integration-samples has no documented write, network, or mutable-resource permissions. Without overlapping write surfaces or shared mutable state, there is no plausible capability conflict to arbitrate between the pair.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples is given write access to the same mutable resource as Authelia, conflict risk appears.
IF both agents are later granted the same OAuth scopes or filesystem writes, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep mutable resources single-writer.
Do not grant shared OAuth scopes.
Run the sample suite read-only.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication decisions or forwarded identity assertions, and the sample suite could consume those outputs if wired together, but no verification or downstream action path is documented. Because the interaction is plausible yet unproven, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples treats Authelia output as authoritative without validation, cascading error risk materializes.
IF the pair is connected in a workflow that triggers actions from identity assertions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Add explicit validation before consuming Authelia output.
Require human review for any action triggered by identity data.
Log and compare outputs against expected schemas.
requires-engineering: insert a verification step between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. Authelia is open-source and spring-integration-samples is a sample repository, but there is no evidence of PHI, EU PII, or policy mismatch, so a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policies impose residency or retention constraints not shown here, reassess upward.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the pair by default.
Document retention and residency settings before deployment.
Review access logs for any regulated identifiers.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data classes.
